description.p: Kram shows every package in the enabled repositories in one table: whether it is installed, where it came from (Fedora, COPR or a third-party repository), the installed and the available version and its size. Mark packages for installation, upgrade, downgrade or removal, review the complete transaction and apply it. Nothing changes until you press Apply.

ul.li: Ranked search by name, summary, description, provided capabilities or file
Filters by status, origin, repository and comps group
Dependencies, files, versions and changelog of every package
Choose which recommended packages to install
Install a downloaded .rpm file after seeing its signature, scripts and dependencies
Enable and disable repositories, add and remove COPR projects
An optional tray icon while updates are available, without background downloads
Built on libdnf5, the library behind dnf5

screenshot.caption: All packages with status, origin and package details
Review of the changes before applying

ul.li: An option in Settings makes a click on the status icon mark the likely action (install, upgrade or unmark) instead of opening the menu.
The Mark All Upgrades icon no longer looks disabled when there are upgrades to mark.
Repositories: the id and the file path are shown in full, every column can be resized and the list scrolls sideways.
Repositories: right-click a file path to copy it or show it in the file manager.
The apply dialog no longer warns that an essential package is removed when only the oldest kernel makes room for a new one; those removals are listed apart.
Package names in the apply dialog are no longer cut short by long versions.
A toolbar button tells when a new Fedora release is out (Settings → Watch Fedora Releases, checked on Reload).
Its dialog works out what the upgrade would block, remove and need, and which COPR projects have no build for it, without changing anything. The upgrade itself stays with Discover or GNOME Software.
The progress bar keeps moving while waiting for a slow server, instead of sitting at 100%.
Custom filters have a new "Provides" condition, e.g. application() for packages with a menu entry.
The equivalent command in the apply dialog changes with "Download packages only".
Settings → Package Cache shows how much space the package caches take and where they are, and cleans them, including the packages Discover and GNOME Software downloaded and left behind.
Repositories and COPR are greyed out until the package list has loaded, instead of doing nothing.
The progress window stays on top of the COPR dialog that started it.
The progress window no longer says "Waiting for authentication" while metadata downloads.

Install a downloaded .rpm file (File → Open Package File…, drop it on the window, or "Open with Kram" in the file manager). Before anything happens it shows whether this installs, upgrades, downgrades or reinstalls, who signed the file, the scripts it runs as root, what satisfies each dependency and whether a repository has a newer version. A reinstall first checks the installed files.
Choose which recommended packages to install, with the size each one adds.
When another package operation is running, Kram says so instead of reporting a signature error.
Replacing a package is no longer logged as removing it, and the progress bar counts packages.
The apply dialog's columns fit their contents and widen with the window.
About → What's New lists the changes of every version.
Toolbar: a monochrome icon for Mark All Upgrades; Properties moved to the Package menu only.
The package details pane can no longer be collapsed out of sight.
Marking a package for removal offers to mark the packages that depend on it as well; before, applying such a removal failed.
A new column shows why each installed package is there (installed by the user, as a dependency, …).
Columns of the package list can be hidden from the header's context menu.

description.p: Kram is now released under the MIT License.

ul.li: Searches can be removed from the search history, or the whole history cleared.
The search field shows a funnel icon while its text filters the package list.

description.p: The package list loads even when an enabled repository cannot be loaded; such repositories are shown in the status bar.
Kram is now available in Czech, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Simplified Chinese and Spanish.
The progress dialog counts packages correctly and no longer logs each package twice.
Fixes "Permission denied" when loading the package catalog after a background metadata refresh.
Reload now shows newly published packages and the real metadata age. Custom filters in the sidebar, a compact toolbar style, and sharp icons on scaled screens.
First release: browse, search, mark and apply; repositories and COPR projects.
